$comment: The sacred-systems registry. These are the code paths that move or could strand user money: the basket LAUNCH system and the basket SWAP/trading system. Any release whose diff touches a path here is a SACRED release: it must name the touched system(s) in its CHANGELOG section (a 'Sacred:' line), declare them in version.json's 'sacred' field, carry an impact of at least 'config' (never 'safe'), and pass the live sacred smoke (npm run smoke:sacred) before it ships. CI re-checks this on every release commit (scripts/sacred-diff.mjs). Editing THIS file is itself a changelog-visible change.

launch.why: Basket creation. A regression here bricks deploys for every visitor of every site built from this kit (failure class: a bad leg route sails through salt-mining, then every deploy reverts on-chain with CREATE2Failed). Since 2026-08-06 launching also MAKES THE FIRST DEPOSIT: a launch that deploys without depositing leaves the basket first-mintable by anyone, and whoever gets there chooses the funding split (contracts measured a 57% loss on the next honest buyer), so the launch batch and its funding case are launch-sacred too.

swap.why: Basket trading (buy/sell). A regression here breaks or misroutes user money on live sites.

shared.why: Sacred to BOTH systems: hook-data encoding + slippage defaults, contract ABIs, the canonical address book, per-chain routing config, fee math, and the build-time config that ARMS the money paths. Added 2026-08-06 after the zero-split incident: the FUNDING SPLIT decides how a buyer's money is divided across legs, so the modules that read, carry or probe it are sacred by definition - a wrong split is a mis-sent payment, not a display bug. They were unregistered while shipping the very bug that proved it.

executor.why: THE LIVE-MONEY SWITCHES AND THE REVIEW RECORD THAT GATES THEM (added 2026-08-07 after an independent review found them absent while a feature toggle was present — F9). allocation.ts's SIMULATED and portfolio-batcher.ts's ZEROEX_COMPOSE_ENABLED are the two constants that decide whether the executor moves real money; review-ledger.json is what gate A10 reads to decide whether the flip is allowed. A one-line edit to any of the three changes what the whole harness permits, so each belongs in a SACRED release with its system named.

dependencyReminder.note: Dependency changes ship as their own releases, never mixed with sacred code changes. A bump of the money-path libraries (viem, wagmi) is treated as sacred even with zero first-party diff: run the sacred smoke and declare it.
